title: Episode 182: C++ Variadic Templates, Swift and More with Doug Gregor

sentences.en: So, when Chris started this off, what was his original vision and intent?
sentences.zh: 那么，当克里斯开始着手这件事时，他最初的愿景和意图是什么？

sentences.en: Was it to create a general purpose systems programming language?
sentences.zh: 是为了创建一个通用的系统编程语言吗？

sentences.en: I see a nod.
sentences.zh: 我看到有人点头。

sentences.en: I am nodding, yes.
sentences.zh: 我在点头，是的。

sentences.en: The overall goal was general purpose systems programming language.
sentences.zh: 总的目标就是通用的系统编程语言。

sentences.en: Would you say that's what Swift has become?
sentences.zh: 你会说这就是 Swift 后来变成的样子吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I think that is what Swift has become, but that's not necessarily what the perception of Swift is.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这正是 Swift 最终成为的样子，但这不一定是人们对 Swift 的普遍看法。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 182, recorded on April 29th, 2024.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 182 期，录制于 2024 年 4 月 29 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we continue our interview with Doug
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天我和我的联合主持布莱斯一起，继续采访道格

sentences.en: Greger, and in this episode, chat about C++, variadic templates, stdtuple, stdvariant, the
sentences.zh: 格雷格尔。在本期节目中，我们聊到了 C++、可变参数模板、stdtuple、stdvariant、

sentences.en: Swift programming language, and more.
sentences.zh: Swift 编程语言等等。

sentences.en: But, actually, this is perhaps a good transition point, because I don't want to talk solely with Doug about concepts.
sentences.zh: 不过，其实这也许是一个很好的切入点，因为我不想只跟道格讨论概念。

sentences.en: I actually want to bring up something that you said to me last year at PLDI, and I'm not sure if you'll remember this, but we were talking about a feature that you worked on
sentences.zh: 我其实想提起你去年在 PLDI 上对我说过的一件事，我不确定你是否还记得，当时我们在讨论你参与过的一个特性

sentences.en: that did end up going into C++11, which was variadic templates.
sentences.zh: 最终确实进入了 C++11，也就是可变参数模板。

sentences.en: And I believe you said something akin to variadic templates was like a perfect feature.
sentences.zh: 而且我记得你说过类似可变参数模板堪称完美特性的言论。

sentences.en: There were no defects.
sentences.zh: 没有任何缺陷。

sentences.en: It's just a perfect, pure thing, and I'm very happy with it.
sentences.zh: 它就是那种完美、纯粹的东西，我对此非常满意。

sentences.en: And I felt a little bit differently, because while variadic templates are a wonderful feature,
sentences.zh: 而我的感受则稍有不同，因为虽然可变参数模板是个绝佳的特性，

sentences.en: and anybody who does not feel that way should look at how tuple was implemented pre-variadic templates.
sentences.zh: 而且任何不这么觉得的人都应该去看看在可变参数模板出现之前 tuple 是怎么实现的。

sentences.en: You can go find it in the old Boost libraries, or the Thrust tuple, a thing that I have had to deal with for many more years than I would like.
sentences.zh: 你可以在旧的 Boost 库里找到它，或者是 Thrust tuple，这是一个我不得不应付的、比我希望的时间还要长得多的东西。

sentences.en: But my objection, my issue with variadic templates is this head-tail pattern that you can't index into them.
sentences.zh: 但我的反对意见、我对可变参数模板的看法在于这种头尾模式，你无法对它们进行索引。

sentences.en: Although, interestingly, last committee meeting, we voted in parameter pack indexing.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，在上次委员会会议上，我们投票通过了形参包索引。

sentences.en: But explain yourself, sir.
sentences.zh: 但请解释一下吧，先生。

sentences.en: Why are variadic templates such a great feature?
sentences.zh: 为什么可变参数模板会是一个如此棒的特性？

sentences.en: I should have known it wasn't safe to talk to you about variadic templates.
sentences.zh: 我早该知道跟你讨论可变参数模板是不安全的。

sentences.en: So, the reason I was so happy with variadic templates, I still like the feature, is it's a pretty tiny extension.
sentences.zh: 所以，我之所以对可变参数模板如此满意——我依然很喜欢这个特性——是因为它是一个非常微小的扩展。

sentences.en: And for a tiny extension, it enables a whole lot of really interesting abstractions.
sentences.zh: 对于一个微小的扩展来说，它促成了大量非常有趣的抽象。

sentences.en: So, at its core, you have one, I guess you have two new things.
sentences.zh: 所以在其核心，你有一个，我想你有两个新东西。

sentences.en: Like, it only introduces two things into the C++ language.
sentences.zh: 就像它只向 C++ 语言引入了两个东西。

sentences.en: What did you just do?
sentences.zh: 你刚才做了什么？

sentences.en: You put the peace sign up for the listener.
sentences.zh: 你给听众比了个和平手势。

sentences.en: You know, Doug was...
sentences.zh: 你知道，道格他……

sentences.en: I had a peace sign for two.
sentences.zh: 我比了个表示二的和平手势。

sentences.en: Doug was...
sentences.zh: 道格他……

sentences.en: Who put his two fingers up, and then a bunch of balloons appeared, you know, floating up around his head.
sentences.zh: 谁举起了两根手指，然后一堆气球就出现了，你知道的，在他脑袋周围飘来飘去。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if there's some birthday sign or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我不确定是不是有什么生日标志或者诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: Maybe they thought you were...
sentences.zh: 也许他们以为你是……

sentences.en: But it's not going to happen on our systems, Connor, because we are both connecting from non-Apple systeMs.
sentences.zh: 但这不会在我们的系统上发生，康纳，因为我们两个连接时用的都不是苹果系统。

sentences.en: And I'm pretty sure that this is an Apple thing.
sentences.zh: 而且我很确信这是苹果的某种功能。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Look at that.
sentences.zh: 你看那个。

sentences.en: That's amazing that it's an Apple feature in a Microsoft product.
sentences.zh: 在一个微软的产品里居然能有苹果的特性，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: Well, it's...
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是……

sentences.en: My understanding of how it works is that it's like a...
sentences.zh: 据我所知它的运作方式就像是一个……

sentences.en: Like, it's an injection.
sentences.zh: 就像是一个注入。

sentences.en: So, it's something that Apple layers on top of the camera feed, and then feeds through to the apps.
sentences.zh: 所以这是苹果在摄像头画面之上叠加的一层效果，然后再传输给各种应用。

sentences.en: So, it's transparent.
sentences.zh: 所以它是透明的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's pretty cool, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话这挺酷的。

sentences.en: It's pretty impressive.
sentences.zh: 相当让人印象深刻。

sentences.en: But the net effect is that we got a party with balloons while we're talking about variadic templates.
sentences.zh: 但最终的效果就是，我们在聊可变参数模板的时候，竟然还伴随着气球派对。

sentences.en: So, I'm pretty happy with that.
sentences.zh: 所以我对此相当满意。

sentences.en: This is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: This is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: The two things that variadic templates added are parameter packs, introduced by the ellipsis, that abstract over any number of parameters.
sentences.zh: 可变参数模板增加的两样东西是：由省略号引入的形参包，它能够抽象任意数量的形参。

sentences.en: Same idea, whether it's template arguments or function parameters.
sentences.zh: 无论是模板实参还是函数形参，都是这个相同的理念。

sentences.en: And pack expansion, which lets you take a pack and expand it out into multiple arguments.
sentences.zh: 还有包展开，它能让你把一个包展开成多个实参。

sentences.en: As a feature, it's really tiny.
sentences.zh: 作为一个特性，它真的很小。

sentences.en: And it wasn't terribly hard to implement.
sentences.zh: 而且实现起来也不是特别难。

sentences.en: So, the initial implementation took about a week or two in GCC, including porting over
sentences.zh: 所以最初的实现只在 GCC 里花了一到两周时间，包括把

sentences.en: tuple, function, and bind libraries and getting them completely working.
sentences.zh: tuple、function 和 bind 库移植过来并让它们完全正常工作。

sentences.en: And so, it's fairly easy to teach.
sentences.zh: 因此它相当容易教给别人。

sentences.en: It's a fairly small extension.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当小的扩展。

sentences.en: And yet, it let us get rid of this horrible limitation on the number of template parameters you could have in a way that I was fairly proud of.
sentences.zh: 然而，它却让我们以一种我颇感自豪的方式，摆脱了对模板参数数量的那个糟糕限制。

sentences.en: Pack indexing is nice.
sentences.zh: 包索引是个好东西。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: So, why didn't we get pack indexing in the first version?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们在第一个版本里没有得到包索引呢？

sentences.en: Why was it like this head-tail sort of pattern to unpack them?
sentences.zh: 为什么解包的时候非得用这种类似头尾的模式？

sentences.en: So, we didn't have pack indexing in the first version, mostly because we couldn't come up with a syntax, which sounds really silly.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在第一个版本里没有包索引，主要是因为我们想不出一个语法，这听起来真的很傻。

sentences.en: But, you know, we tried several different things.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我们尝试了好几种不同的东西。

sentences.en: And you couldn't really subscript.
sentences.zh: 而且你确实无法进行下标访问。

sentences.en: That wouldn't work.
sentences.zh: 那样行不通。

sentences.en: And I think we tried subscript with the leading dot, like x dot subscript, you know, open square bracket something.
sentences.zh: 我想我们尝试过带前导点的下标，比如 x 点下标，你知道的，左方括号什么的。

sentences.en: And that was hitting problems with the preprocessor.
sentences.zh: 而那遇到了预处理器方面的问题。

sentences.en: And essentially, we sort of got tired of looking for a syntax for a feature that wasn't strictly necessary, right?
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，我们有点厌倦去为一个并非绝对必要的特性寻找语法了，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you can implement this directly.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以直接实现它。

sentences.en: Why couldn't you subscript?
sentences.zh: 为什么你就不能用下标呢？

sentences.en: Well, because x subscript with an i, that is completely reasonable if your pack x had a bunch of values in it that were all, like, vectors or something, or arrays.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为 x 带 i 的下标，如果你的包 x 里面有一堆值全都是像向量或数组之类的东西，那完全是合理的。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对的，对的。

sentences.en: The syntax that we settled on that we have in C++26 is dot, dot, dot subscript.
sentences.zh: 我们最终确并在 C++26 中采用的语法是点、点、点下标。

sentences.en: Okay, sure.
sentences.zh: 好吧，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That will work.
sentences.zh: 那会起作用的。

sentences.en: That may have provoked antibodies had we tried to add it to the proposal at that point in the C++OX time frame.
sentences.zh: 如果在 C++0X 的那个时间节点上我们试图把它加入提案，那可能会引发抗拒。

sentences.en: To be fair, it would have been almost impossible to have foreseen at that time how widely used parameter packs would have been and how important the indexing would end up being.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，在那个时候几乎不可能预见到参数包会被广泛使用到什么程度，以及索引最终会变得多么重要。

sentences.en: I think the same can be said of constexpr when, you know, constexpr is like the C++ case study
sentences.zh: 我认为对于 constexpr 也可以这么说，当，你知道的，constexpr 就像是 C++ 的案例研究

sentences.en: in incremental evolution where we shipped a very minimal restricted form of constexpr in C++11
sentences.zh: 关于渐进式演进的案例，我们在 C++11 中发布了一个非常最小化、受限形式的 constexpr，

sentences.en: and it's slowly grown over the past decade with every release us allowing more things in constexpr,
sentences.zh: 并且在过去十年里，随着每个版本的发布它都在慢慢成长，允许在 constexpr 中使用更多东西，

sentences.en: we're making more things constexpr at the point now that you can have constexpr vectors and
sentences.zh: 我们让越来越多的东西变成 constexpr，以至于发展到今天你可以拥有 constexpr 向量和

sentences.en: strings and that constexpr today is a very different beast than it was back then and it's
sentences.zh: 字符串，而且今天的 constexpr 与过去相比已经面目一新，并且

sentences.en: used, you know, it's a whole new form of metaprogramming that has arisen around constexpr replacing
sentences.zh: 它被广泛使用，你知道的，围绕 constexpr 已经涌现出了一种全新的元编程形式，它在某些方面取代了

sentences.en: type-based metaprogramming in a ways that I don't think the people who originally worked on constexpr could have ever really imagined.
sentences.zh: 基于类型的元编程，这是当年最初参与 constexpr 开发的人们绝对无法想象的。

sentences.en: And as you say, variadic templates, a, you know, very important and signature feature of C++11, at the time, it may not have seemed like that because it was this very easy and
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，可变参数模板，一个，你知道的，C++11 非常重要且标志性的特性，当时它可能看起来并不起眼，因为它是一件非常轻松且

sentences.en: simple thing to do.
sentences.zh: 简单的事情。

sentences.en: You said it was pretty straightforward to put into the language, it was pretty straightforward
sentences.zh: 你说过把它放进语言里相当直接，实现起来也相当直接，

sentences.en: to implement and the full impact of it may not have been known or realized at the time.
sentences.zh: 而它的全部影响在当时可能并未被完全认知或意识到。

sentences.en: No, and our goals when we did it were very much around these libraries.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且我们当时做这事的目标在很大程度上正是围绕着这些库。

sentences.en: So std function was mine.
sentences.zh: 所以 std function 是我的。

sentences.en: I was working with Yako Yarvi who did std tuple and we were both really frustrated by this dumb limit that we had.
sentences.zh: 我当时正与实现 std tuple 的亚科·亚尔维（Jaakko Järvi）合作，我们俩都对我们所拥有的那个蠢限制感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: You could only have 10 or 20 or whatever the implementation defined limit was.
sentences.zh: 你只能有 10 个、20 个或者实现定义的任何限制。

sentences.en: Values that worked.
sentences.zh: 那些能工作的值。

sentences.en: And so we wanted this feature to make our libraries better.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要这个特性来让我们的库变得更好。

sentences.en: And that, that was kind of the scope we imagined that, you know, only library designers doing this kind of thing would end up using variadic templates.
sentences.zh: 而且，那差不多就是我们设想的范围，你知道的，只有做这种事情的库设计者最终才会使用可变参数模板。

sentences.en: So keeping it sort of smaller was a benefit.
sentences.zh: 所以把它保持得较小是一个优势。

sentences.en: So, so tuple actually is an interesting one because I, I, for a long time have been a proponent of the, um, uh, expose things as, uh, as, uh, struct in class, um, abstractions.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以 tuple 其实是一个很有意思的例子，因为我，我长期以来一直是那种，嗯，主张将事物暴露为，嗯，作为 struct 和 class 抽象的人。

sentences.en: Um, and the, the, the way, the way I like to explain, explain this to people is like C arrays and C++ are weird because they don't really behave like other things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我向人们解释这一点的方式就像是 C 风格数组和 C++ 很奇怪，因为它们的行为真的不像其他东西。

sentences.en: There's a whole bunch of caveats.
sentences.zh: 这里面有一大堆注意事项。

sentences.en: When you have an array object, you can't return them from functions.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有一个数组对象时，你无法从函数中返回它们。

sentences.en: Um, they have all these, like when you pass them in as parameters to functions, there's all these pointer decay things that happen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们有所有这些，比如当你把它们作为参数传给函数时，会发生所有这些指针衰退的事情。

sentences.en: Um, and like std array is better because it's a normal thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像 std array 更好，因为它是一个正常的东西。

sentences.en: It is a, you know, it's a struct.
sentences.zh: 它是一个，你知道的，它是一个结构体。

sentences.en: So therefore it follows all the basic rules of what a struct is.
sentences.zh: 因此它遵循结构体的所有基本规则。

sentences.en: And that's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事。

sentences.en: We like things that sort of like behave like the other things.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢那些表现得像其他东西的事物。

sentences.en: And that's one of the reasons why in sort of modern C++ design, we like to expose things as, uh, even things that are language features.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么在某种现代 C++ 设计中，我们喜欢将事物暴露为——即使是语言特性也一样。

sentences.en: We like to expose them through the library, even things like, you know, reflection, like the metadata type is exposed as a library type.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢通过库将它们暴露出来，甚至连诸如，你知道的，反射之类的事情，比如元数据类型也是作为库类型暴露的。

sentences.en: Um, uh, and things like, you know, tuple and, uh, uh, variant get exposed as library types because then they behave like all other, uh, class instruct types.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有诸如 tuple 和 variant 之类的事情，它们作为库类型被暴露出来，因为这样它们就能表现得像所有其他 class 和 struct 类型一样。

sentences.en: Um, with that said, um, uh, just so many hours in years of people's time have been spent on, you know, making tuple work or making variant work.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，嗯，人们已经把无数的小时和年头花在了，你知道的，让 tuple 正常工作或者让 variant 正常工作上。

sentences.en: In tuple, aside from std git being a little bit ugly, tuple's not so bad.
sentences.zh: 在 tuple 中，除了 std get 稍微有点丑陋之外，tuple 其实没那么糟。

sentences.en: Um, variant I think is less pleasant to, to work with though.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过我觉得使用 variant 没那么令人愉快。

sentences.en: The real place where tuple's painful is more on the implementation side of things.
sentences.zh: tuple 真正让人痛苦的地方其实更多在实现这一侧。

sentences.en: And I just wonder, would we have been better off with a language, uh, tuple?
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，如果我们有一个语言层面的 tuple，会不会更好呢？

sentences.en: Was that something that was considered at the time?
sentences.zh: 当时有人认真考虑过这件事吗？

sentences.en: I don't remember it being seriously considered at the time.
sentences.zh: 我不记得当时有谁认真考虑过它。

sentences.en: And now tuple has a pretty long history.
sentences.zh: 而现在 tuple 已经有了相当长的历史。

sentences.en: So it was a boost library.
sentences.zh: 所以它曾是一个 boost 库。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you know, it and function were the first two papers that were voted into the C++ technical
sentences.zh: 你知道，它和 function 是前两篇被投票通过并收录进 C++ 库扩展技术报告的论文，

sentences.en: report on library extensions, which is like the first thing the committee did after C++ 98.
sentences.zh: 那就像是委员会在 C++98 之后做的第一件事。

sentences.en: Yeah, the TR.
sentences.zh: 对，就是 TR。

sentences.en: The TR, right?
sentences.zh: TR，对吧？

sentences.en: The good old TR.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的旧 TR。

sentences.en: Eventually came into C++ OX.
sentences.zh: 最终它进入了 C++ OX。

sentences.en: And I, there wasn't a whole lot of appetite for language extensions at that time.
sentences.zh: 而且我记得当时对语言扩展并没有太多的热情。

sentences.en: So I don't know that people would have really considered it as a language feature.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道人们是否真的会把它当成一个语言特性来考虑。

sentences.en: And then part of the thing is what you said there's, you know, tuple as a library works pretty well.
sentences.zh: 然后部分原因正如你所说，你知道的，作为库的 tuple 运作得相当好。

sentences.en: So if we get a nice pattern matching facility, then it'll work pretty well, probably quite, quite well in C++.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们能有一个优秀的模式匹配设施，那么它就会运作得很好，在 C++ 中大概会相当、相当不错。

sentences.en: Uh, variant is a completely different story though.
sentences.zh: 不过，variant 完全是另一回事了。

sentences.en: I do not, uh, love using variant.
sentences.zh: 我并不，嗯，很喜欢使用 variant。

sentences.en: I tend to hand code my own, uh, discriminated union types.
sentences.zh: 我往往会自己手写我自己的，嗯，可辨识联合类型（discriminated union types）。

sentences.en: This is one of those things where, uh, in Swift, we got it right.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种，嗯，在 Swift 中我们把它做对了的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, this is at the point where, uh, if someone came up with a feature in the C plus plus committee, myself or later, uh, Richard Smith could go ahead and try to hack it up
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正是在这个时候，嗯，如果有人在 C++ 委员会中提出一个特性，我自己或者后来的理查德·史密斯就会继续尝试在 Clang 中

sentences.en: in Clang.
sentences.zh: 把它拼凑出来。

sentences.en: It's very possible that your digit separator story was this exactly that we went and tried
sentences.zh: 很有可能你的数字分隔符故事正是如此，我们去在 Clang 中尝试

sentences.en: to hack it up in Clang and found some ambiguity or something, um, even though I don't remember it.
sentences.zh: 拼凑它，然后发现了一些歧义或类似的东西，嗯，尽管我不记得了。

sentences.en: And so, but as this was happening, uh, we were also adding more support to Clang for, for
sentences.zh: 所以，但正当这一切发生时，嗯，我们还为 Clang 增加了对其他事物的更多支持，比如，嗯，针对 Objective-C，这是苹果在 C 家族中支持的另一种语言。

sentences.en: other things like, um, for objective C, which is the other language Apple, you know, supports in the C family.
sentences.zh: 我们增加了自动引用计数，以试图提高该语言的内存安全性。

sentences.en: We added automatic reference counting to try to improve the memory safety of the language.
sentences.zh: 我们增加了自动引用计数，以试图提高该语言的内存安全性。

sentences.en: But, uh, we really realized that C plus plus and just the C family of languages had some fundamental limitations that we could never fix.
sentences.zh: 但，呃，我们确实意识到 C++ 以及 C 语言家族有一些永远无法修复的根本局限性。

sentences.en: Some of those are around memory safety.
sentences.zh: 其中一些局限性与内存安全有关。

sentences.en: I don't necessarily want to go down that rabbit hole, but you know, our view was that these
sentences.zh: 我倒不一定要陷入那个细节的泥潭，但你知道，我们的看法是这些

sentences.en: are unsolvable problems in, in the language as we have it, or that solving them would change the language so much that it wouldn't still be the same.
sentences.zh: 在现有的语言中是无法解决的问题，或者说解决这些问题会极大地改变这门语言，以至于它就不再是原来的那个语言了。

sentences.en: And the other problem is that you can't really remove anything from C plus plus.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，你基本上无法从 C++ 中移除任何东西。

sentences.en: And so you're stuck with a lot of decisions that we would not have made early on.
sentences.zh: 因此，你不得不背负很多我们在早期根本不会做出的决定。

sentences.en: And so, um, we decided to, it was time to go and build a new modern native language based on all we had learned about, you know, language design and compiler design.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，我们决定是时候去构建一门全新的、现代的原生语言了，它基于我们所学到的一切，你知道的，包括语言设计和编译器设计。

sentences.en: And so Chris Blattner totally started it in secret.
sentences.zh: 于是克里斯·拉特纳（Chris Lattner）完全在秘密中启动了这项工作。

sentences.en: And then after a bit of hacking, uh, he looped in several of us to go and join him.
sentences.zh: 在经过了一段时间的黑客式开发后，呃，他把我们其中的好几个人拉进来加入他。

sentences.en: So I'm committer number two, uh, to the, the repository for Swift and have been working on it ever since, including, you know, the generic system, uh, was initially my design.
sentences.zh: 所以我是 Swift 仓库的二号提交者，呃，从那以后就一直致力于它的开发，包括，你知道的，泛型系统最初就是由我设计的。

sentences.en: I've also worked on the concurrency system, the macro system, and most other aspects of the language over the years.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，我还参与了并发系统、宏系统以及该语言的大多数其他方面的开发。

sentences.en: So when, when Chris started this off, um, what was his original vision and intent?
sentences.zh: 那么当，当克里斯开始着手这件事时，呃，他最初的愿景和意图是什么？

sentences.en: Was it to create a, a general purpose systems programming language?
sentences.zh: 它是为了创建一个，一个通用的系统编程语言吗？

sentences.en: I see an, I see a nod.
sentences.zh: 我看到，我看到一个点头的动作。

sentences.en: I am nodding.
sentences.zh: 我在点头。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The, the, the, the overall goal was general purpose systems programming language.
sentences.zh: 总的，总的，总的，总的目标就是通用的系统编程语言。

sentences.en: Would you say that's what Swift has become?
sentences.zh: 你会说这就是 Swift 已经变成的样子吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think that is what Swift has become, but that's not necessarily what the perception of Swift is.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这就是 Swift 已经变成的样子，但这不一定是人们对 Swift 的普遍看法。

sentences.en: Yes, I would, I would, I would tend to agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我，我，我会倾向于赞同。

sentences.en: I think people tend to think of Swift as that language that you write your Apple, your iOS apps in, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们往往把 Swift 视为那种用来编写你的苹果、你的 iOS 应用程序的语言，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, but so, okay, so maybe you can, you can tell us a little bit more about Swift and, uh, Swift's design and specifically what makes it a general purpose language and not just
sentences.zh: 呃，但是，好吧，所以也许你可以，你可以向我们多介绍一点关于 Swift 和，呃，Swift 的设计，特别是究竟是什么让它成为一门通用语言，而不仅仅是

sentences.en: that app language.
sentences.zh: 那种应用程序语言。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Uh, so, I mean, what does systems programming language actually mean is, is right.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以，我的意思是，系统编程语言实际上意味着什么，这说得对。

sentences.en: Cause I can define it a lot of different ways.
sentences.zh: 因为我可以从很多不同的方式来定义它。

sentences.en: And so it's tough.
sentences.zh: 所以这很艰难。

sentences.en: So the things that we look at are, um, as a language, it needs to have abstractions so that you can build good libraries because any system of any size is architected as a set
sentences.zh: 所以我们关注的事情是，呃，作为一门语言，它需要具备抽象能力，以便你能构建好的库，因为任何规模的系统都是作为一组

sentences.en: of libraries.
sentences.zh: 库来架构的。

sentences.en: Uh, it needs to have a compilation model that, um, admits efficient code.
sentences.zh: 呃，它需要有一个编译模型，呃，能够生成高效的代码。

sentences.en: So in our view, this meant it had to compile to native code.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们看来，这意味着它必须编译为原生代码。

sentences.en: We, we couldn't accept requiring a JIT, uh, behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们无法接受在底层要求一个 JIT，呃。

sentences.en: And the design has to be such that you can scale your program.
sentences.zh: 并且它的设计必须能够让你的程序进行扩展。

sentences.en: So I've had a hard time articulating exactly what this means, but you know, if your language
sentences.zh: 所以我很难确切地表达这意味着什么，但你知道，如果你的语言

sentences.en: depends on having to see every bit of source code everywhere and compiling it all together, you aren't going to be able to scale up to a larger system.
sentences.zh: 依赖于必须看到随处可见的每一行源代码并将它们全部编译在一起，你就无法扩展到更大的系统。

sentences.en: You have to be able to ship separate software components with stable interfaces that can evolve over time.
sentences.zh: 你必须能够发布带有稳定接口的独立软件组件，这些组件可以随着时间的推移而演进。

sentences.en: And so, um, our view is those are the main ingredients.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，在我们的看法中，这些就是主要的组成部分。

sentences.en: And the, the last piece that we cared about a lot was, is related to memory safety, but it's not memory safety.
sentences.zh: 而我们非常关心的最后一点，与内存安全有关，但它并不是内存安全。

sentences.en: So it was really, we wanted to make it such that it was easy to get to correct code.
sentences.zh: 所以它真正想要做的是，我们要让编写出正确的代码变得轻而易举。

sentences.en: So the compiler and its type system should support you in getting your code, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，编译器及其类型系统应该支持你写出正确的代码。

sentences.en: Things like undefined behavior shouldn't happen.
sentences.zh: 诸如未定义行为之类的事情不应该发生。

sentences.en: And the type system should encourage good patterns that help you write correct code and deal with
sentences.zh: 并且类型系统应该鼓励良好的编程模式，帮助你编写正确的代码并处理

sentences.en: erroneous cases and so on in a way that, you know, it's obvious when you look at the code, what it's doing and that that's what it actually is doing under the hood.
sentences.zh: 错误的情况等等，其方式是，你知道的，当你查看代码时，它在做什么是一目了然的，并且它在底层实际做的就是这个。

sentences.en: And, and so that, that's kind of the overall dream of Swift.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是 Swift 的整体愿景。

sentences.en: Um, and you can see this play out in, uh, how the, the language is actually designed.
sentences.zh: 呃，你可以从，呃，这门语言实际的设计方式中看出这一点。

sentences.en: So, uh, things you're probably familiar with, for example, in Swift, we push value semantics everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，你可能很熟悉的事情是，例如在 Swift 中，我们到处推行值语义。

sentences.en: We love value semantics, right?
sentences.zh: 我们热爱值语义，对吧？

sentences.en: And value semantics have this wonderful property that if you have a value and you make a copy of it, the original value and its copy are completely independent.
sentences.zh: 值语义有一个美妙的特性：如果你有一个值并制作了一个它的副本，那么原始值和它的副本是完全独立的。

sentences.en: Nothing you can do to one will change the other.
sentences.zh: 你对其中一个做的任何事情都不会改变另一个。

sentences.en: This is so good for local reasoning because you can just reason about the code that's on your screen.
sentences.zh: 这对于局部推理太棒了，因为你只需推理屏幕上的代码即可。

sentences.en: You don't have to think about, well, someone else might have an alias to my data structure over here.
sentences.zh: 你不需要去想，好吧，这里的其他人可能拥有指向我的数据结构的别名。

sentences.en: That's going to create some spooky action at a distance and affect my code.
sentences.zh: 那将会产生一些诡异的远距离作用并影响我的代码。

sentences.en: And when you have that basis of value semantics, which like runs throughout Swift, then you can make immutability that really works and say, okay, well, most of the time you're not
sentences.zh: 而当你拥有了贯穿 Swift 的值语义这一基础时，你就可以实现真正管用的不可变性，并说，好吧，大多数时候你其实并不会

sentences.en: changing things.
sentences.zh: 改变事物。

sentences.en: So let's make it easy to do immutability in the language and make that sort of the default view that things should be mutable unless you really, really want to make it mutable.
sentences.zh: 因此，让我们在语言中轻松实现不可变性，并将这种观点设为默认设置——除非你真的、真的想要让它可变，否则事物应该是不可变的。

sentences.en: And then those mutations will be local.
sentences.zh: 然后那些修改也将会是局部的。

sentences.en: When did automatic reference counting become the memory management story of choice for Swift?
sentences.zh: 自动引用计数是什么时候成为 Swift 首选的内存管理方案的？

sentences.en: Or does that just come from the Objective-C background or was it a principled choice?
sentences.zh: 还是说这仅仅源自 Objective-C 的背景，亦或是一个原则性的选择？

sentences.en: No, it was actually principled choice.
sentences.zh: 不，这其实是一个原则性的选择。

sentences.en: So it was certainly true that Objective-C had a convention-based manual reference counting scheme that we then codified in Clang to make it automatic.
sentences.zh: 所以，固然 Objective-C 拥有基于约定的手动引用计数方案，我们后来将其在 Clang 中规范化以使其变为自动的。

sentences.en: When we started Swift, we looked at the options.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始开发 Swift 时，我们审视了各种选项。

sentences.en: I mean, the main options there were traditional garbage collection or something like automatic reference counting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那里的主要选项是传统的垃圾回收或类似于自动引用计数的技术。

sentences.en: And they're interesting and have different trade-offs.
sentences.zh: 它们都很有趣，并且有不同的权衡。

sentences.en: I think the easy answer probably would have been, ah, let's do a traditional garbage collector.
sentences.zh: 我想简单的回答可能是，啊，我们来做个传统的垃圾回收器吧。

sentences.en: But there's a couple of things that worked against that.
sentences.zh: 但有几件事情对这个方案不利。

sentences.en: One, we'd had sort of a poor experience with trying to do garbage collection for Objective-C.
sentences.zh: 第一，我们在尝试为 Objective-C 做垃圾回收时有过不太好的体验。

sentences.en: There was an attempt.
sentences.zh: 曾经有过这种尝试。

sentences.en: It didn't really work out very well.
sentences.zh: 结果并不是很好。

sentences.en: But there's a reason for that, which is when you're interoperating with a C stack, you have some of your software written in C and some of it written in another language.
sentences.zh: 但这是有原因的，那就是当你在与 C 栈进行互操作时，你的一些软件是用 C 编写的，而另一些是用其他语言编写的。

sentences.en: You can't trust C to behave the way you want it to from the perspective of a garbage collector.
sentences.zh: 从垃圾回收器的角度来看，你无法信任 C 会按你希望的方式行事。

sentences.en: And you see how hard this is in any language that has garbage collection and also has a native interface to C.
sentences.zh: 你也能看到，在任何既有垃圾回收机制又有到 C 的原生接口的语言中，这一点是多么困难。

sentences.en: And with Swift, we knew that one of our key features had to be really good interoperability with C so that we could start incrementally moving the world over.
sentences.zh: 而在 Swift 中，我们知道我们的关键特性之一必须是与 C 的极佳互操作性，这样我们才能开始逐步把全世界的代码迁移过来。

sentences.en: Having garbage collector would have made that really hard.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个垃圾回收器会使这一点变得非常困难。

sentences.en: That's one of the points.
sentences.zh: 这是其中一点。

sentences.en: The other point that I think is really important is that the great thing about reference counting
sentences.zh: 我认为非常重要的另一点是，引用计数最棒的地方在于

sentences.en: is you can locally optimize it away when you have more information.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有更多信息时，你可以在局部将其优化掉。

sentences.en: It becomes a compiler optimization problem.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一个编译器优化问题。

sentences.en: You set up your calling convention so that you know where the reference counts are supposed to be maintained.
sentences.zh: 你设置你的调用约定，以便你知道应该在何处维护引用计数。

sentences.en: But if you have some performance critical code where you absolutely cannot handle the cost of reference counting, you can force the optimizer to look harder, add more annotations
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你有一些对性能要求极高、绝对无法承受引用计数成本的代码，你可以强迫编译器更深入地进行优化，在语言中添加更多注解

sentences.en: to the language, whatever it takes to eliminate the reference counting just in that place without affecting anything else in the system.
sentences.zh: ——无论需要什么——从而仅在那个地方消除引用计数，而不会影响系统中任何其他部分。

sentences.en: So it has this really nice property that you can do local optimizations to improve performance without throwing out the model.
sentences.zh: 所以它有一个非常好的特性，即你可以通过局部优化来提升性能，而无需抛弃整个模型。

sentences.en: Finally, you don't need a runtime except for like we have retain and release.
sentences.zh: 最后，除了我们有的 retain（保留）和 release（释放）之外，你甚至不需要运行时。

sentences.en: That's it, right?
sentences.zh: 就是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: A couple of instructions.
sentences.zh: 几条指令而已。

sentences.en: It's an atomic basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上是个原子操作。

sentences.en: And so you need very little runtime support to make this model work.
sentences.zh: 所以要使这个模型工作，你只需要非常少的运行时支持。

sentences.en: And so that lets you scale your language down to run it in environments where you would never consider having a garbage collector running.
sentences.zh: 这使得你可以将你的语言向下扩展，使其能够在那些你绝不会考虑运行垃圾回收器的环境中运行。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And so that gave us the option to actually say, well, you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以这给了我们一个选项，可以实际地说，嗯，你知道吗？

sentences.en: This is actually reasonable to use down in a kernel or down in firmware somewhere where you don't, you could never do a GC and you would have to essentially switch the model.
sentences.zh: 在内核中或在某个固件里使用这个其实是合理的，而在那种地方你绝不能使用 GC，你基本上不得不切换模型。

sentences.en: We don't have to change the model.
sentences.zh: 我们不必改变模型。

sentences.en: We just have to make sure it's optimized well in those places.
sentences.zh: 我们只需确保它在那些地方得到了很好的优化。

sentences.en: And it also gives you determinism, right?
sentences.zh: 而且它还赋予了你确定性，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, you don't, yeah.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你不用，对。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That is the other thing I should have mentioned.
sentences.zh: 这是我本该提到的另一件事。

sentences.en: It gives you determinism of you know at the end of your scope or when you stop using a value that the reference count is going to drop and it will go away.
sentences.zh: 它赋予了你确定性：在你的作用域结束时，或者当你停止使用一个值时，你知道引用计数会下降并且它会消失。

sentences.en: So you can reason about it better than you can with a garbage collector.
sentences.zh: 因此，与垃圾回收器相比，你可以更好地对其进行推理。

sentences.en: I've always been, well, it's one of the reasons I've always been a fan of Swift has been Arc
sentences.zh: 我一直，嗯，这也是我一直是 Swift 的粉丝的原因之一就是 ARC

sentences.en: because I, for many years, worked on the HPX runtime, which is an HPC parallel programming runtime.
sentences.zh: 因为我多年来一直致力于 HPX 运行时的开发，这是一个 HPC 并行编程运行时。

sentences.en: And, uh, HPX is, uh, uh, relies entirely upon reference counting and has this, um, distributed,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，HPX 是，呃，完全依赖于引用计数，并且拥有这种，呃，分布式

sentences.en: uh, reference counting mechanism, um, where it's based on, uh, you know, you get a number of reference count tokens and then as the thing moves, you can split them.
sentences.zh: 呃，引用计数机制，呃，它基于，你知道的，你获得一定数量的引用计数令牌，然后随着事物移动，你可以拆分它们。

sentences.en: And so you don't have to have that much reference counting traffic.
sentences.zh: 所以你不需要产生那么多的引用计数流量。

sentences.en: And that's what I'd spent a lot of my early work on.
sentences.zh: 这就是我早期花了很多精力去研究的领域。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, one of the things that I came to appreciate in that time was in particular,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，你知道的，我在那个时期开始欣赏的一点是，特别是

sentences.en: when you're working on a concurrent system, you, you need to have some form of managed lifetimes, um, because you don't, you, you cannot solely rely upon, you know, new and
sentences.zh: 当你正在开发一个并发系统时，你，你需要某种形式的生命周期管理，呃，因为你不能，你不能仅仅依靠，你知道的，new 和

sentences.en: delete, and you don't have this scoping.
sentences.zh: delete，并且你没有这种作用域。

sentences.en: So you can't just rely on something like unique pointer.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能只依赖像 unique_ptr 这样的东西。

sentences.en: You, you need some way of, uh, managing the lifetimes of objects.
sentences.zh: 你，你需要某种方式来，呃，管理对象的生命周期。

sentences.en: And I really believe that reference counting's the best option.
sentences.zh: 我真的坚信引用计数是最好的选择。

sentences.en: Um, it's deterministic, I think gives you the best performance.
sentences.zh: 呃，它是具有确定性的，我认为它能给你带来最好的性能。

sentences.en: Um, it's straightforward to reason about.
sentences.zh: 呃，它直观易懂。

sentences.en: The only thing you really have to concern yourself with is the potential risk of cycles.
sentences.zh: 你真正需要担心的唯一事情是循环引用的潜在风险。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, in my years of dealing with reference counting systems, uh, it's never been a, a major, a major, uh, issue.
sentences.zh: 呃，但是，呃，在我处理引用计数系统的这些年里，呃，这从来都不是一个，主要的，主要的，呃，问题。

sentences.en: Um, I've run into it a couple of times, but, uh, it, it, to me, and it's, it's, it's, I think there's, I think, I think the automatic reference counting is something that almost
sentences.zh: 呃，我碰到过几次，但是，呃，对我来说，而且它，它，它，我认为有，我认为，我认为自动引用计数是某种几乎
